files.what_breaks_if_deleted: An install without a frozen lockfile could resolve a different dependency tree than the one reviewed, and an unaudited high-severity advisory could ship silently — CI's --frozen-lockfile flag and the verify:audit high-severity gate would both be unproven.
A transitive dependency's postinstall script could run arbitrary code on every install (dev machine and CI runner alike) with no allowlist catching it.

A dependency with an install script that is neither allow-listed nor explicitly ignored fails a fresh frozen install in CI and in the merge gauntlet, or worse, silently runs a script nobody reviewed — this is the exact class the original sec-051-postinstall-allowlist.test.ts missed, because it only asserted the allowlist's shape and never drove pnpm's own build-script gate against a truly fresh node_modules the way CI does.
A floating base image tag could silently change the base under a passing build, and a container running as root would turn a container escape into host access, with nothing catching either.
An unpinned GitHub Action (tag/branch ref instead of a commit SHA) is a supply-chain write to CI that nothing would catch.

A leak scan that exists but is not wired into pnpm verify is a script nobody runs; without this test a planted or non-ASCII term, token-boundary regression, unset/invalid/zero-term list, empty explicit scope, unreadable target, or traversal of excluded/reparse-point output could escape the scanner contract.

A leak scan wired to a subset of the public surface passes while a customer term sits in a root config file or a workflow that ships to the public repo (review-WP-001-2.md finding b, attempt-3 R-3 remediation).
TLS could go unenforced on the database hop, or HSTS could be absent from the base headers config, while the encryption claim in the bid stayed unchallenged.
Real SMS/voice could be left enabled by configuration in the demo environment, sending a synthetic reminder to a real phone number the first time a reviewer clicks a demo journey.
The long-lived worker could regain database-wide schema creation or pg-boss could expose ambient function access instead of relying on owner-provisioned, object-scoped rights.
